original_question: Does there exist a Hessian nilpotent formal power series P(z) in C[[z]] that is not a polynomial and for which the Vanishing Conjecture fails? Equivalently, can one find a non-polynomial Hessian nilpotent formal power series over C such that the quantities Delta^m(P(z)^(m+1)) do not eventually vanish, or prove that no such example exists?
target_in_paper: Open Problem 5.2 in Section 5: the paper asks whether there exists a Hessian nilpotent formal power series over C that is not a polynomial and for which the Vanishing Conjecture fails. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/85371))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly targets the paper's Section 5 formal-power-series variant of the Vanishing Conjecture, not the original quartic homogeneous polynomial statement of Conjecture 1.1. It also correctly keeps the two essential restrictions from Open Problem 5.2: P must be Hessian nilpotent and P must lie in C[[z]] but not in C[z]. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/85371))
missing_details: Specify the variables explicitly: z=(z_1,...,z_n) for some finite n>=1, and the ambient rings are C[z_1,...,z_n] and C[[z_1,...,z_n]]. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/85371))
Define Hessian nilpotent explicitly: Hes P=(∂^2P/∂z_i∂z_j) is a nilpotent n x n matrix over C[[z_1,...,z_n]]. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/85371))
Define the Laplace operator explicitly as Delta=sum_{i=1}^n ∂^2/∂z_i^2. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/85371))

Spell out what 'the VC fails for P' means in this setting: there is no N such that Delta^m(P^{m+1})=0 for all m>=N; equivalently, Delta^m(P^{m+1}) is nonzero for arbitrarily large m. This is the negation of the eventual vanishing in Conjecture 1.1. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/85371))

Make explicit that Open Problem 5.2 has no homogeneity, degree-4, or polynomial-degree restriction; those belong to Conjecture 1.1, not to this Section 5 formal-series question. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/85371))

If one wants to invoke Proposition 1.2 to replace the HN condition by Delta^m(P^m)=0 for all m>=1, one must additionally assume o(P)>=2; that auxiliary order hypothesis is not stated in Open Problem 5.2 itself. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/85371))

The paper phrases the problem as an existence question ('Find ..., if any'); the extra wording 'or prove that no such example exists' is mathematically natural but is not the paper's exact formulation. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/85371))
refined_question: Does there exist an integer n>=1 and a Hessian nilpotent formal power series P(z) in C[[z_1,...,z_n]] but not in C[z_1,...,z_n]], where Hes P=(∂^2P/∂z_i∂z_j) is nilpotent and Delta=sum_{i=1}^n ∂^2/∂z_i^2, such that for every N>=1 there exists m>=N with Delta^m(P(z)^{m+1}) != 0? ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/85371))
justification: The nearest official target is Open Problem 5.2, not Conjecture 1.1 itself. Conjecture 1.1 gives the original VC for homogeneous degree-4 HN polynomials, while Section 5 explicitly asks whether the VC can fail over C for a HN formal power series that is not a polynomial. Section 1.2 flags this exact issue as the motivating question of Section 5 after Proposition 5.1 shows that, in positive characteristic, the VC holds for all HN formal power series. Proposition 1.2 is relevant background for an alternate HN criterion only under the extra assumption o(P)>=2, and Theorem 1.3 explains why the quantities Delta^m(P^{m+1}) are the natural objects to track. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/85371))
